Nested cross-validation with racing inside

Source: R/nested-tune-race.R
nested_tune_race.Rd

nested_tune_race_anova() and nested_tune_race_win_loss() estimate how well a model tuned with finetune's racing functions performs on new data. They run the loop of nested_tune_grid(), with a race on each outer fold's inner resamples.

Usage

nested_tune_race_anova(object, ...)

# Default S3 method
nested_tune_race_anova(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'model_spec'
nested_tune_race_anova(
  object,
  preprocessor,
  resamples,
  ...,
  param_info = NULL,
  grid = 10,
  metrics = NULL,
  event_level = "first",
  eval_time = NULL,
  select = selection_rule()
)

# S3 method for class 'workflow'
nested_tune_race_anova(
  object,
  resamples,
  ...,
  param_info = NULL,
  grid = 10,
  metrics = NULL,
  event_level = "first",
  eval_time = NULL,
  select = selection_rule()
)

nested_tune_race_win_loss(object, ...)

# Default S3 method
nested_tune_race_win_loss(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'model_spec'
nested_tune_race_win_loss(
  object,
  preprocessor,
  resamples,
  ...,
  param_info = NULL,
  grid = 10,
  metrics = NULL,
  event_level = "first",
  eval_time = NULL,
  select = selection_rule()
)

# S3 method for class 'workflow'
nested_tune_race_win_loss(
  object,
  resamples,
  ...,
  param_info = NULL,
  grid = 10,
  metrics = NULL,
  event_level = "first",
  eval_time = NULL,
  select = selection_rule()
)

Arguments

object

A workflows::workflow() with at least one parameter marked with tune::tune(), or a parsnip model specification.

...

On the generic, the arguments of the method. On a method, pass control = finetune::control_race() here to set the control. Name every argument after ....

preprocessor

A formula or recipe, when object is a model specification.

resamples

A nested resampling design from nested_resamples() or rsample::nested_cv().

param_info

A dials::parameters() object or NULL. If none is given, a parameters set is derived from other arguments. Passing this argument can be useful when parameter ranges need to be customized.

grid

A data frame of tuning combinations or a positive integer. The data frame should have columns for each parameter being tuned and rows for tuning parameter candidates. An integer denotes the number of candidate parameter sets to be created automatically.

metrics

A yardstick::metric_set(), or NULL for tune's default set. Under every rule but "desirability", the first metric selects each fold's candidate, so put the metric you report first. The Bayes, race and annealing searches also steer on it. Every metric is scored on the outer folds.

event_level

"first" (the default) or "second". It names which level of a two-class outcome is the event. It applies to the inner tuning run and the outer scoring fit alike.

eval_time

A numeric vector of evaluation times for a censored regression model, or NULL (the default) to leave the choice to tune. Times that are not numeric, empty, missing, negative or not finite are an error. Zero, repeated and unordered times are passed on to tune.

select

A selection_rule() that each outer fold uses to pick its candidate. The default is tune::select_best() on the first metric.

Value

A nested_results, as nested_tune_grid() describes.

Details

Each outer fold scores every candidate in grid on the first burn_in inner resamples. It then drops the candidates that are clearly worse than the best, by a repeated-measures ANOVA or by a model of pairwise wins and losses. The rest are scored on the remaining resamples. nested_tune_grid() documents what the loop functions share, such as the design, what the estimate describes, the seeds, failed folds and parallel execution.

Both functions need finetune, on each parallel daemon as well. nested_tune_race_anova() also needs lme4, and nested_tune_race_win_loss() needs BradleyTerry2.

Each fold's .inner_metrics holds every candidate its race scored, including the ones it dropped. In that table, n is the number of inner resamples each candidate was scored on, so a dropped candidate has a smaller n. A candidate that failed on every inner resample is missing, and its failure is in .notes. The recorded grid, attr(res, "grid"), is the design the race was offered, exactly as given.

An inner design with an apparent split, such as the one bootstraps(apparent = TRUE) makes, is an error here, though finetune runs it. A race drops candidates on the score of each split, and an apparent split is scored on the rows the model trained on. The other tuners accept the split, because tune leaves it out of its estimates. nested_workflow_map() checks for it before its first workflow runs.

Differences from calling finetune directly

A finetune::control_race() passed through ... as control reaches the inner race in every fold, and nested_final_fit() runs again with it. Its settings differ from a direct call as follows.

Forced: allow_par. The inner race and the outer fit run with allow_par = FALSE, because the outer folds carry the parallelism.

Settable as its own argument: event_level. Set the level with the event_level argument, as on nested_tune_grid(). A control left at the default level, "first", takes the argument's level. A control set to another level than the argument's is an error. grid and eval_time are the racing functions' own arguments, not control settings.

Refused: none. No setting is refused on its own. A control of another class is an error, even a control_grid() that finetune accepts.

Passed through: burn_in, alpha, num_ties, randomize, verbose_elim, verbose, pkgs, parallel_over, workflow_size. Each reaches the race as given:

  • burn_in, alpha, num_ties and randomize act on each fold's race as in a direct call. With randomize = TRUE, the default, the fold's tuning seed sets which resamples the burn-in uses.

  • A burn_in that is not smaller than some fold's number of inner resamples is an error before any fold runs. The default burn_in is 3, so a design with three inner resamples needs a burn_in of 2 or fewer.

  • verbose and verbose_elim print from each fold, and only a serial run shows the output.

pkgs, parallel_over and workflow_size behave as on nested_tune_grid().

These settings were read from finetune 1.3.0. The oldest finetune this package accepts can lack workflow_size in control_race().

Kept from the outer fit: save_pred, extract. As on nested_tune_grid(), the outer fit's predictions and extracts are kept as .predictions and .extracts when you ask for them. The inner race's own are still discarded.

Not returned: save_workflow. The nested run does not keep the inner tuning results, so this setting returns nothing there. nested_final_fit() keeps its own tuning run as $tuning, which holds what the setting saved.

Inert: backend_options. Options for a parallel backend, with no backend to reach at allow_par = FALSE.

See also

nested_tune_grid(), nested_resamples(), nested_final_fit(), nested_tune_bayes(), finetune::tune_race_anova(), finetune::tune_race_win_loss()

Examples

data(mtcars)

rec <- recipes::recipe(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars) |>
  recipes::step_pca(recipes::all_predictors(), num_comp = tune::tune())
wf <- workflows::workflow(rec, parsnip::linear_reg())

# A race needs more inner resamples than its burn-in, so five inner folds.
set.seed(1)
folds5 <- nested_resamples(
  mtcars,
  outside = rsample::vfold_cv(v = 2),
  inside = rsample::vfold_cv(v = 5)
)

set.seed(2)
res <- nested_tune_race_anova(
  wf,
  folds5,
  grid = data.frame(num_comp = 1:4),
  control = finetune::control_race(burn_in = 2, verbose_elim = FALSE)
)
collect_metrics(res)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err
#>   <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl>
#> 1 rmse    standard   2.98      2  0.459 
#> 2 rsq     standard   0.747     2  0.0691

# Every candidate the first fold's race scored, and on how many inner
# resamples: `n` below 5 is a candidate the race eliminated.
res$.inner_metrics[[1]]
#> # A tibble: 8 × 7
#>   num_comp .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err .config        
#>      <int> <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>          
#> 1        1 rmse    standard   2.42      5  0.576  pre1_mod0_post0
#> 2        1 rsq     standard   0.861     5  0.0627 pre1_mod0_post0
#> 3        2 rmse    standard   2.81      5  0.414  pre2_mod0_post0
#> 4        2 rsq     standard   0.847     5  0.0630 pre2_mod0_post0
#> 5        3 rmse    standard   2.86      5  0.365  pre3_mod0_post0
#> 6        3 rsq     standard   0.828     5  0.0482 pre3_mod0_post0
#> 7        4 rmse    standard   3.26      2  0.693  pre4_mod0_post0
#> 8        4 rsq     standard   0.693     2  0.0868 pre4_mod0_post0
